review_notes: I read the whole file, which has two theorems and no simp attributes. I searched Mathlib and the LeanPool repo for competing rules and for how the lemmas are used. The related Mathlib lemmas are `Nat.sum_range_choose` (the row sum `∑ m ∈ range (n+1), n.choose m = 2^n`) and `Nat.sum_Icc_choose`. Neither matches the `∑ l ∈ range g, l.choose m` shape, so there is no overlapping simp rule. Every use in the repo (`Recursion.lean`, `Weighted.lean`, `ChainBound.lean`) calls `sum_range_choose_real` through an explicit `rw`, so no downstream simp call needs it. I do not recommend tagging either theorem `@[simp]`. The ℕ form would be a reasonable simp lemma, since its right-hand side is smaller. But no source shows a use that would benefit, so adding it would be a speculative annotation. The ℝ cast form would be a weaker candidate because simp's cast-pushing lemmas could interfere with it. The proof's own `simp` and `ring` calls are routine. I found no cycle, bad orientation or unwanted-expansion issue. I could not run Lean, so I have not tested the simp behaviour.
